chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Abbas ibn Aamir, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he went to a man, took off his sandal, then said: 'Take off your sandals, for the sandal, when it is taken off, gives rest to the two feet'.
ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette and reason for removing footwear according to the Imam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) models the etiquette of removing footwear by leading the action, thereby emphasizing the social and physical comfort of the practice. He explicitly links the removal of shoes to the relief of the feet, framing this daily act as a means of physical ease and consideration for others. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the Prophet and Imams as practical exemplars of modesty and comfort in mundane interactions.
